item.title: Polynomial Spectral Gap Estimates for Finitely Differentiable Quasi-Periodic Schr\"odinger Operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.26977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove polynomial upper bounds on spectral gaps of quasi-periodic Schr\"odinger operators with small $C^{k}$ potentials and Diophantine frequencies. For sufficiently large $k$, the decay exponent is $k-34\tau$, where $\tau$ is the Diophantine exponent. We construct examples with lower bounds along infinitely many gap labels, showing that the leading coefficient $1$ of $k$ is asymptotically optimal. The proof uses quantitative reducibility and the Moser-P\"oschel argument.
item.dc:creator: Ao Cai, Yang Gao, Jiawei He

item.title: A periodic Anderson--Bernoulli model with infinitely many spectral gaps
item.description: arXiv:2610.27160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the (almost-sure) spectrum of a periodic Anderson--Bernoulli model may enjoy infinitely many gaps. In particular, this shows that Schr\"odinger operators associated with transitive subshifts of finite type do not necessarily have finite-gap spectra. This resolves a pair of open problems posed by Damanik and the first named author. The main mechanism is the construction of a transverse heteroclinic connection within the class of Schr\"odinger transfer matrices, together with a scale-matching argument to produce a sequence of invariant multicones.
item.dc:creator: Jake Fillman, William Wood

item.title: The Spectrum of the Discrete Mathieu Operator with Nonreal Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.27487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the discrete Mathieu operator with nonreal coupling in the large-period limit, using complex WKB methods for analytic finite-difference equations. We obtain quantization formulas in different regions of the complex energy plane. Away from the corners of the image of the classical symbol, these formulas involve cosines of classical action integrals with small analytic corrections to the actions. Near each corner, we derive a uniform quantization formula involving the reciprocal Gamma function. The quantization formulas constrain spectral accumulation to curves determined by the competing exponential terms. Numerical computations illustrate the resulting spectral geometry.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Klopp, Izak Oltman

item.title: P\'olya's conjecture for Dirichlet eigenvalues of spherical shells and Aharonov--Bohm annuli
item.description: arXiv:2610.27707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish strict Dirichlet P\'olya inequalities for spherical shells in every dimension $d\ge2$ and for every radius ratio. The inclusive eigenvalue counting function lies strictly below the leading Weyl term at every positive energy; consequently, each eigenvalue strictly exceeds its Weyl prediction, with multiplicities included. We also prove the same strict inequality for the Aharonov--Bohm operator on planar annuli at arbitrary flux. In dimension two, the nonmagnetic result gives a fully analytic proof of the planar annulus theorem of Filonov, Levitin, Polterovich and Sher (J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2026). The common ingredient is a lattice-point bound for the shell action, uniform in the starting point of a tail and in the lattice translation. Quadrature for the inverse action controls the change of convexity caused by the inner boundary. The tail estimate supplies the hypothesis of the known dimension-reduction argument for balls, while lattice translations represent the magnetic flux. Laptev's product argument yields corresponding strict bounds on products of shells and nonempty bounded open sets.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Li

item.title: Explicit sharp gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincar\'e inequality and fundamental gaps for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.27281v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove the gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincar\'e inequality with explicit constants on bounded convex domains for any $1<p<\infty$. These estimates control the distance to the optimizers in the strongest possible norm with the optimal stability exponent $\max\{2,p\}$, exhibiting the same phenomenon initially observed by Figalli and Zhang [FZ22a] for the $L^p$-Sobolev inequality. As a result, we also confirm the conjecture posed by Fleckinger-Pell\'e and Tak\'a\v{c} [FPT02, Section 8]. We then apply the inequality to obtain positive fundamental gap estimates in terms of the inradius for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian.
item.dc:creator: Nurgissa Yessirkegenov, Amir Zhangirbayev

item.title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, I: radiation conditions and a Rellich-type theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.27885v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the negative Laplacian on the half-space $\mathbb{R}^n_+$, $n \ge 3$, subject to a constant impedance (Robin) boundary condition with $\alpha > 0$. The boundary then carries a bound transverse mode, and at each energy $E > 0$ the system propagates two channels with the distinct wavenumbers $\sqrt{E}$ and $\sqrt{E+\alpha^2}$: bulk waves decaying like $|x|^{-(n-1)/2}$ and surface waves decaying like $|x'|^{-(n-2)/2}$. The two rates are not comparable pointwise. Each is critical for the Agmon-H\"ormander space $\mathcal{B}^*$, however. This Part I treats the flat boundary, and its purpose is to develop, at that endpoint, the scattering theory of the two channels in full. We prove a limiting absorption principle $\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}^*$, construct the generalized Fourier transform, derive an expansion of the resolvent at infinity in which the two channels appear in a single relation, characterize the solutions of $\mathcal{B}^*$ growth, and compute the scattering matrix. The radiation condition is imposed on the solution itself, with no decomposition into channels, and is shown to be equivalent to the vanishing of the incoming data. The main result is a Rellich-type theorem whose hypotheses are imposed only near infinity and which forces both channels to vanish simultaneously. The surface channel turns out to be rigid: its block of the scattering matrix is the identity and carries no information about $\alpha$, so that on the band $-\alpha^2 < E < 0$ the scattering matrix is trivial. The bulk block, by contrast, determines $\alpha$.
item.dc:creator: Michiyuki Watanabe

item.title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.28026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Ferrari-Dominguez

item.title: A Quantitative Robin Faber-Krahn Inequality in Terms of Eigenfunction Distance
item.description: arXiv:2610.28032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a quantitative stability estimate for the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian with positive Robin boundary conditions. For every open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ of prescribed volume, we prove that \[ \lambda_{1,\beta}(\Omega)-\lambda_{1,\beta}(B) \geq c\|u_\Omega-u_B\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^n)}^4, \] where $B$ is a ball achieving the Fraenkel asymmetry of $\Omega$, and $u_\Omega$ and $u_B$ are nonnegative, $L^2$-normalized first Robin eigenfunctions, extended by zero outside their respective domains. The constant $c>0$ depends only on the dimension, the Robin parameter, and the prescribed volume. The exponent $4$ is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Nitsch, Cristina Trombetti, Federico Villone

item.title: Fourier Decomposition and E-Eigenvalues of Hypergraph Polynomials over Finite Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $H=(V,E)$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph with polynomial $f_H(\bm{x})=\sum_{e\in E}\prod_{v\in e}x_v$. For a finite abelian group $G$ and a subgroup $S$ of $G$, the $k$-partite Cayley hypergraph $K$ has $k$ disjoint vertex parts, each indexed by $G$, and $\{(1,g_1),\ldots,(k,g_k)\}$ is an edge if and only if $g_1+\cdots+g_k\in S$. For $k=2$, $K$ is isomorphic to the Bi-Cayley graph associated with $G$ and $S$. For $k\ge3$, we use character theory to express $f_K$, under a complex unitary change of variables, as a sum of exactly $[G:S]$ nonzero monomials in pairwise disjoint sets of variables. This yields a direct sum decomposition whenever $S$ is a proper subgroup of $G$. When $G=\Z_2^m$, this transformation is real and orthogonal, enabling us to determine the complete sets of complex E-eigenvalues and Z-eigenvalues of the adjacency tensor of $K$.
item.dc:creator: Yan-Hong Bao, Yi-Zheng Fan, Lili Liao

item.title: On the spectrum of the biharmonic Steklov operator with Neumann boundary conditions acting on forms of the unit Euclidean ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.28181v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the spectrum of the biharmonic Steklov operator with Neumann boundary conditions acting on differential $p$-forms over the unit Euclidean ball. We apply it to test how far one of Kuttler-Sigillito inequalities is from being optimal.
item.dc:creator: Rodolphe Abou Assali

item.title: The concentration conjecture for Dirac--Coulomb operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.28193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the concentration conjecture for the three-dimensional Dirac operator with mass $m>0$ and an attractive Coulomb potential generated by finitely many point charges. For a fixed total charge $G\in(0,1]$, the lowest eigenvalue in the spectral gap is at least $m\sqrt{1-G^2}$, with equality precisely when all the charge is concentrated at one point. The critical one-center operator is understood as its distinguished extension. The result also extends to arbitrary nonnegative finite charge measures. The proof uses a strict two-center estimate for the weighted free Dirac resolvent and a Birman-Schwinger comparison. We establish the two-center estimate through an auxiliary axial operator, combining a zero-energy bound and a scalar resolvent estimate with a radial decomposition, an angular Schur complement, and exact polynomial inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Habib Ammari, Jiayu Qiu

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Lower bounds for self-adjoint Sturm-Liouville operators
item.description: arXiv:2212.09837v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note we provide estimates for the lower bound of the self-adjoint operator associated with the three-coefficient Sturm-Liouville differential expression $$ \frac{1}{r} \left(-\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dx} p \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dx} + q\right) $$ in the weighted $L^2$-Hilbert space $L^2(\mathbb R; rdx)$.
item.dc:creator: Jussi Behrndt, Fritz Gesztesy, Philipp Schmitz, Carsten Trunk

item.title: On the Genericity of the Spectrum Intervalization for Multi-Frequency Quasiperiodic Schr\"{o}dinger Operators
item.description: arXiv:2602.07445v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper proves a genericity conjecture by Goldstein, Schlag, and Voda[Invent. Math.\textbf{217}(2019)] for multi-frequency quasiperiodic Schr\"{o}dinger operators. Specifically, we show that for almost all coefficients of real trigonometric polynomial potentials, the spectrum forms a single interval under strong coupling conditions. This confirms a long-standing intuition by Chulaevky and Sinai[Comm.Math.Phys.\textbf{125}(1989)] that the spectrum typically intervals for generic potentials, and extends the existence results of Goldstein et al. to a full measure setting. Our proof relies on tools from differential topology, measure theory, and analytic function theory.
item.dc:creator: Daxiong Piao

item.title: Canonical forms for boundary conditions of self-adjoint odd-order differential operators
item.description: arXiv:2602.21234v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is useful to have canonical forms of boundary conditions in the study of the eigenvalues of boundary value problems and associated numerical applications. In [J. Appl. Anal. Comput., 2024, 14(4), {1854--1868}], a canonical form is given for self-adjoint differential operators of even order, with eigenvalue parameter dependent boundary conditions. In this article, we derive canonical forms for the remaining case, namely: for self-adjoint $(2n+1)$-th order differential operators with eigenvalue parameter dependent boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Yorick Hardy, Bertin Zinsou

item.title: Spectral and Schr\"odinger estimates restricted to submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2511.02012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with nonpositive sectional curvature and smooth bounded geometry. We prove logarithmic spectral projection estimates restricted to uniformly embedded submanifolds. On surfaces with pinched negative curvature, we also prove frequency-independent $L^2\to L^3$ Schr\"odinger restriction estimates on compact geodesic segments for times $c\lambda^{-1}\log\lambda$. If such a surface is even asymptotically hyperbolic, the $L^2\to L^q$ spectral estimates on complete nontrapped geodesics, for $q>2$, gain the square root of the window width. The high-frequency Schr\"odinger estimate holds for all times on these surfaces, both on compact segments and on complete nontrapped geodesics. Under a regularity assumption at the spectral threshold, the all-time estimate holds on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace.
item.dc:creator: Zhexing Zhang

item.title: Quantitative Landis-type result for Dirac operators
item.description: arXiv:2602.16049v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study quantitative unique continuation at infinity for Dirac equations with bounded matrix-valued potentials. For the massless Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we establish a Landis-type estimate showing that the vanishing order of any nontrivial bounded solution of $( \mathcal{D}_n + \mathbb{V} ) \varphi = 0$ satisfies a lower bound of order $\exp(-\kappa R^{2} (\log R)^{2})$ as $|x|=R\to \infty$; the quadratic growth in the exponent is sharp, in view of previous known results. Our proof follows a Bourgain--Kenig type approach based on a Carleman inequality for Dirac operators which relies on a local H\"older regularity result, which we also prove. In two dimension, we obtain improved quantitative estimates under symmetry assumptions on the potential $\mathbb{V}$ and for real-valued solutions. Finally, we also derive qualitative Landis-type results for Dirac equations with decaying potentials, including critical decay rates.
item.dc:creator: Ujjal Das, Luca Fanelli, Luz Roncal

item.title: Finite-Dimensional Type I von Neumann Algebras in PyTorch: A GPU-Accelerated Framework for Random Block-Diagonal Operators
item.description: arXiv:2606.15882v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: torch_vn_algebra is a PyTorch library for numerical work with finite-dimensional von Neumann algebras, i.e. direct sums of matrix algebras. These algebras are central to operator algebra theory and, via commutants of symmetries, describe quantum systems with conserved charges or superselection rules. To our knowledge, no numerical software treats them as a data type with their centre, family of traces, conditional expectations, inclusions and functional calculus. The library fills the gap between computer algebra (exact but small-scale) and quantum simulators (large-scale but limited to Hilbert-space matrices): it handles batches of operators on CPUs and GPUs with automatic differentiation, and converts operators, states and channels. Key features: Compact tensor representation: 4D tensor (B, C, kmax, kmax), where B is batch size (e.g. Monte Carlo samples), C is the number of summands, and kmax is the max block size, enabling batched GPU processing. Lazy evaluation: matrix data materialized only on access, avoiding memory waste. Random operator generation: custom eigenvalue distributions; Haar, SU(n), COE, CSE unitary ensembles. Functional calculus and spectral methods: matrix absolute value, square root, inverse, entropy via SVD; automatic switch between exact diagonalization (block size up to 256) and power iteration for extreme eigenvalues. Three trace functionals: Tr_blunt (sum of block traces), Tr_norm (dimension-normalized), tau_vN (faithful normal tracial state). Performance: on a Tesla P100 GPU, processing 20,000 samples of 100x100 operators yields up to 30x speedup over traditional CPU workflows. Availability: open-source at https://gitlab.com/a.hobukob/von_neumann_type_i/
item.dc:creator: Irina Nikolaeva, Andrej Novikov

item.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the computation of transform pairs
item.description: arXiv:2606.25252v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a unified methodology that integrates spectral theory, Riemann-Hilbert problems, and inverse scattering theory for the construction and numerical evaluation of transform pairs associated with linear variable-coefficient partial differential equations. The approach combines analytical formulae with numerical methods for ordinary differential equations and Riemann-Hilbert problems, yielding a hybrid analytical-numerical strategy for working with these transforms. Results are presented for transforms arising in the Dirac equation, demonstrating accurate computations, even in the presence of discontinuous coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Kaitlynn Lilly (Department of Applied Mathematics, University of Washington), Thomas Trogdon (Department of Applied Mathematics, University of Washington)

item.title: A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
item.description: arXiv:2608.05077v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by Tartar's vision of a \emph{point-free} theory, we derive explicit norm resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting technique and solve a generalized Sylvester equation that controls the commutator between the differential structure and the highly oscillatory material properties. This abstract perspective unifies stationary, non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions between these media--and their respective convergence rates--are entirely captured by the behavior of the spectral measures of the microscopic and macroscopic derivative operators near zero frequency.
item.dc:creator: Thuyen Dang, Yuliya Gorb, Silvia Jim\'enez Bola\~nos

item.title: Localization near the edge for the lattice Anderson-Bernoulli model on general dimension
item.description: arXiv:2609.30209v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Anderson tight-binding model is a fundamental model of quantum transport and localization in disordered media. Solving a problem left open by Bourgain and Kenig, this paper proves Anderson localization near the bottom of the spectrum for the lattice Anderson model with Bernoulli potential, in any dimension $d\ge 2$. The proof uses the multiscale framework of Fr\"ohlich-Spencer and Bourgain-Kenig, and the main new ingredient is a probabilistic discrete unique continuation principle (PDUC) for the discrete Schr\"odinger equation. This PDUC is established via a bootstrap argument and a key probabilistic lemma proved by adaptively revealing the random potential.
item.dc:creator: Linjun Li, Shihe Liu, Lingfu Zhang
